title: Renaming and removing
question: A name moves, a directory will not go while it has names in it, and a file goes when its last name does. What does ext4 do?
text: A name moves, a directory will not go while it has names in it, and a file goes when its last name does. Four calls on ext4.
1. Renaming within one directory: [ext4_rename](1:ext4_rename) changes the entry's name from "a.txt" to "b.txt"; the inode stays as it is.
2. Removing the directory: [ext4_empty_dir](2:ext4_empty_dir) asks whether it is empty. It is not ("b.txt" is in it), so the call fails with ENOTEMPTY.

3. Removing the file: [ext4_delete_entry](3:ext4_delete_entry) takes the name out of the directory block, and since it was the file's only name and nobody has it open, [ext4_free_inode](3:ext4_free_inode) frees the inode.
4. Now the directory is empty: [ext4_free_blocks](4:ext4_free_blocks) gives its block back to the block bitmap, and its inode is freed too.
Try: [open b.txt before removing it](try:1): the name goes, but the inode stays until the close, which is where `ext4_free_inode` runs then. Or [rename across directories](try:2), to /mnt/b.txt.
tries: renameat2(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/dir/a.txt", AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/dir/b.txt", 0); int fd = openat(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/dir/b.txt", O_RDONLY); unlinkat(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/dir/b.txt", 0); close(fd)
